meta.title: Nvidia: The Platform, the Price Umbrella and the Balance Sheet
meta.dek: Revenue is now guided to grow about 75% next year, the stock is a third off its high, and the founder resigned last week. Every large buyer now has a second chip in volume. What does $163 assume, and is that enough?
meta.price_note: Nov 17, 2026, 6:09 PM EST, after hours, after the Q3 FY2027 release (regular-session close $155.46)
meta.type: Fabless AI-infrastructure platform (accelerators, systems, networking, software)

verdict.sentence: Nvidia has just raised next year's growth outlook to about 75%, yet after a one-third fall from its high and its founder's resignation the stock trades at about 10× next year's pre-print consensus EPS; my probability-weighted case, which assumes share falls toward 58% and revenue goes flat after FY2028, returns [[pw_return]] a year at [[price]], just over the 13% hurdle: Initiate, probability-fragile.
verdict.breaks_if: The FY2028 outlook is cut below 70% growth or receivables pass 70 days of sales, hyperscale revenue falls two quarters running while Broadcom's AI revenue keeps its guide, or non-GAAP gross margin breaks below the 71% floor management set. Any of these says the share-break case is arriving, and each moves 10–15 points from Base to Bear.
verdict.moat: Wide; narrowing at the largest buyers
verdict.next: Q4 FY2027 ~late Feb 2027 (test 1) · CEO search · Hugging Face close
verdict.price_implies: a little below my Base (EPS ≈[[Priced-in.eps]] in FY2032 for 10%/yr)

call: The market is pricing FY2028 as close to the peak. At [[price]], a 10% return needs FY2032 EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]] at 16 times, a little below my Base of [[Base.eps]], and my Base already has revenue going roughly flat after the guided jump to about $740 billion, as Google's TPU, AMD's Helios and Broadcom's custom chips take share at the largest buyers. What I think the price has slightly wrong is how much is left after that: even with share falling from about 83% of spending to about 58% and gross margin to 69%, buybacks and cash returns compound EPS at [[Base.cagr]] a year, and the Bull, a platform that holds two-thirds of a growing market, is worth [[Bull.value]]. Weighted, the value is [[pw_ev]] and the return [[pw_return]], so the price that returns 13% is [[entry]]. The verdict is probability-fragile: the break-even Bear probability is [[breakeven_bear]] against the 25% I assign, so one notch more pessimism on share, demand or the post-Huang roadmap turns it into a Watch. The first check, the FY2028 outlook, came back raised on November 17; the number that settles it over a year is hyperscale revenue against Broadcom's AI revenue.

tests.claim: That FY2028 is the year management says it is, paid for in cash.
tests.test: Q4 FY2027 release and call (about late February 2027): the FY2028 outlook held at 70% growth or better (from about 75% now) and days sales outstanding at 70 or below (64 at Q3).
tests.if_fail: 15 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]] / Hold**, entry ≤[[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That share bleeds rather than breaks at the hyperscalers.
tests.test: Hyperscale revenue grows sequentially in Q4 FY2027 and Q1 FY2028 (reported about late February and late May 2027), as the CFO said it would reaccelerate in Q4 with Vera Rubin supply. Fail: two consecutive sequential declines while Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue meets its own guide.
tests.if_fail: 10 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]] / Hold**, entry ≤[[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That the price umbrella holds while memory costs rise.
tests.test: Non-GAAP gross margin of at least 71.0% in Q4 FY2027 and at least 72.0% in Q1 FY2028 (management guided a bottom of 71–72% in Q4, then 72–73% in FY2028 as price increases take effect in Q1).
tests.if_fail: 10 points Base → Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]] / Hold**, entry ≤[[test3.entry]].

five_year.note: Cycle position: early-to-mid upcycle in AI data-center spending, with FY2023 (the year to January 2023) as the last trough: revenue flat and operating margin 16% after a crypto and gaming inventory correction. Invested capital = equity + debt + operating leases − cash and marketable securities `[Derived]`; FY2026 includes about $12.9B of equity securities and $20.8B of goodwill, so operating ROIC is higher. NOPAT uses a notional 15% tax. FY2026 reinvestment is mostly working capital (receivables, inventory, supply prepayments) and strategic investments, not plant. ROIC passes the 20% test in four of five years and ROIIC and reinvestment pass, but the runway test fails in my own Base, where growth is exhausted after FY2028, so I do not flag Nvidia as a high-ROIIC compounder. Splits: 4:1 in July 2021 and 10:1 in June 2024. return_math.price_implied: At 10%, spot needs EPS of [[Priced-in.eps]] in FY2032 at 16×, a little below my Base ([[Base.eps]]): revenue near $690 billion, roughly the FY2028 guide held flat for four years, at a 58% operating margin. At 13% it needs [[Hurdle.eps]], a fifth of the way from my Base to my Bull.
return_math.epv: Earnings power with no growth: FY2026 operating income of $130.4B taxed at 15% and capitalized at 10% is ≈$1.11T, plus ≈$23B of net cash, ≈$47 a share. On FY2027's ≈$267B of operating income it is ≈$2.25T, ≈$93 a share. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits at FY2027 earnings power, and spot is about 1.7× it.
return_math.base_rate: FY2027 revenue of ≈$410B sits in the >$25B bucket. The Bull's ≈23% nominal growth (≈20% real) was achieved over five years by about 2% of companies this size, and none started this large; most of it is the guided, supply-committed FY2028. The Base's ≈11% nominal (≈8.5% real) was achieved by roughly 20%. Credit Suisse HOLT, 1950–2015 ([Base Rate Book](https://sorfis.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/The-Base-Rate-Book-Integrating-the-Past-to-Better-Anticipate-the-Future-September-2016.pdf)). 3P: Bull Plausible, Base and Bear Probable.
return_math.terminal_growth: Implied perpetual growth on earnings at 10%: Bull [[Bull.g]], Base [[Base.g]], Bear [[Bear.g]], all below the 5.15% ten-year Treasury yield (FRED, Nov 13, 2026).
return_math.year_ten: In the Base the business is not growing at year ten: it is a replacement cycle in which installed gigawatts are refreshed every four to six years and Nvidia holds about half, and the 16× multiple is carried by buybacks and cash returns, not growth.
return_math.rr_note: The downside is a cyclical bust at a normal multiple, not a broken company; the Bear still earns $163B in FY2032.
